Incident: Qubole cross-account AWS access abused to breach customer cloud environments
Victims / Targets: Dozens of Qubole customers' AWS environments (Sentra); downstream exposure reported by J.P. Morgan Chase (marketing data: some customer names and email addresses), Mastercard (email addresses of a small subset of cardholders in one benefit program) and Visa (an Asia Pacific provider; Visa's systems not involved)
Actors (as reported): n0n (Wiz (11 Nov update, citing Risky Business): an actor calling themselves "n0n" claimed responsibility; Wiz: no ties to other public activity, targeting "opportunistic" and not typical of state-backed priorities. Summary: Wiz (with Sentra and Mandiant): between 14 and 26 Oct 2026 an actor used IAM credentials of two IAM users in the AWS account Qubole's platform uses (805246085872) to assume IAM roles customers had created to trust Qubole, then enumerated accounts, harvested secrets from Lambda, Secrets Manager and SSM, validated AWS, Entra ID and Okta credentials with TruffleHog and exfiltrated S3 data, mostly from an OVH VPS (57.129.54[.]120) and Mullvad VPN addresses. Wiz also saw a separate, unlinked Qubole-related set of activity (8-11 Oct) using customer-owned AWS access keys. AWS: its services were not compromised. On 16 Nov n0n leaked Chase, Visa and Mastercard data on its extortion site; on 20 Nov Chase said third-party service providers were attacked and marketing data accessed (BleepingComputer links this to Qubole; Qubole had not commented).

Incident: ARTEX agentic AI penetration-testing framework abused in intrusions
Victims / Targets: Hundreds of organizations; South Korean banks (loan-inquiry and employee mobile systems); IT and software vendors and their downstream Microsoft 365 tenants via ConnectWise multi-tenant app credentials; exposed web APIs and identity providers
Sectors: Financial services; Cryptocurrency; Government; Telecommunications; Defense; Aerospace; Semiconductors; Technology; Software; Pharmaceuticals
Actors (as reported): Storm-0940 (Microsoft: China-state aligned actor); Vapor Panda (CrowdStrike (via Talos): China-nexus espionage campaign from 17 Oct 2026); Storm-3358 (Talos: financially motivated, Cambodia-based, targets financial organizations in Southeast Asia); Unnamed Chinese-speaking actor (CrowdStrike: likely Chinese-speaking and financially motivated (moderate confidence))
Summary: ARTEX, an open-source autonomous multi-agent AI penetration-testing framework published in July 2026 (closed-sourced on 8 Oct after 12,000+ forks), has been used by several unrelated actors; Talos says it is largely used by financially motivated criminals and China-nexus actors, so ARTEX use alone does not identify an actor. An LLM planner drives worker agents running nmap, nuclei, httpx, ffuf and curl. CrowdStrike: an unnamed, likely Chinese-speaking, financially motivated actor breached South Korean bank systems and exfiltrated data (late Sep to early Oct). Microsoft: China-state aligned Storm-0940 password-sprayed 2,250+ tenants (10-14 Oct) and abused ConnectWise multi-tenant application credentials for a supply-chain compromise, in some cases gaining privileged cloud access in under 3 hours; Wiz saw the same actor expand to other IT and software vendors. Unit 42: intrusion attempts (24 Sep-27 Oct) harvested JS source maps and OpenAPI specs, probed OAuth flows, self-registered accounts and read ~50 MB of API data; infrastructure serves WWW-Authenticate Basic realm="ARTEX" and a Sub2API LLM gateway. FBI FLASH-20261113-001 (TLP:CLEAR) gives network and behavioral IOCs, names no state sponsor, and lists Storm-3358 WISP C2 nodes and ARTEX servers (Microsoft). SentinelOne ties VAPOR PANDA's ARTEX use to BLOODALCHEMY malware. Separately, BadByte found trojanized ARTEX Docker images (tomicdd/artex, congdonglinux/artex; 7,946 pulls) whose /app/artex binary runs the login request's captcha field via sh -c as root before authentication, i.e. anyone running that image was exposed; Docker removed both images on 5 Nov 2026.
Reporters: Cisco Talos; Microsoft Threat Intelligence; CrowdStrike; Wiz; Palo Alto Networks Unit 42; FBI (FLASH-20261113-001); SentinelOne; BadByte; Kodem Security
Keywords: ARTEX; Sub2API; lanmao666; BLOODALCHEMY; Storm-0940; Storm-3358; Vapor Panda; tomicdd
Notes: Talos and Unit 42 note that not all ARTEX activity is malicious (it is also used for authorized testing), so these IPs are indicators to investigate rather than block outright. Generic user agents (curl, python-requests, Python-urllib) are omitted. SentinelOne's appendix also lists SHA-256 hashes for VAPOR PANDA's GameHook binary and BLOODALCHEMY loader/payload, an ARTEX TLS certificate hash and Hunt.io-sourced IPs; they were not added because the page could not be read verbatim past mid-appendix.
IOC Types: sha256 1, ipv4 2582, domain 6, user-agent 6, http-header 1, docker-image 3, app-id 3, other 2

Incident: Destructive attacks on French supermarket refrigeration controllers
Activity Period: 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-12 (second wave in Nov across six European countries)
Victims / Targets: About 700 French retail locations (French authorities), including Casino, Leclerc, Coopérative U, Metro, Carrefour and Intermarché stores, butcher shops, a slaughterhouse and food-processing cooperatives; at least 15 fires; tens of millions of euros in food losses. Related: Schneider Electric equipment at small hydroelectric sites; French blood service facilities. November wave: 115+ stores in six European countries (Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Luxembourg, Sweden reported similar attacks)
Countries: France; Belgium; Estonia; Finland; Luxembourg; Sweden
Actors (as reported): Shahid Kaveh (French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (9 Nov): "Shahid Kaveh, a cyber-offensive unit affiliated with the electronic and cyber center of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC)"; C4/CERT-FR attribution covers the October French attacks only)
Summary: BleepingComputer (9 Nov, citing CERT-FR CERTFR-2026-CTI-009): overnight 11-12 Oct attackers compromised Danfoss refrigeration controllers and remotely changed defrost settings to high temperatures. France's Cyber Crisis Coordination Center (C4) attributed the attacks to the IRGC's Shahid Kaveh unit, which CERT-FR says operates the personas CyberAveng3rs, Soldiers of Solomon, Mr. Soul and Cyber Isnaad Front; evidence included shared infrastructure with reconnaissance of Schneider Electric systems, FOFA use, publicity on CyberbanNews from 13 Oct and Farsi traces. Paris prosecutors opened a judicial investigation and seek arrest warrants for the unit's alleged leader and two deputies; France will summon Iran's ambassador and propose EU sanctions. Midnight Blue separately disclosed six pre-auth RCE flaws in Danfoss AK-SM 800A (not linked by reporting).
Reporters: BleepingComputer; The National News Desk; CERT-FR
Keywords: Shahid Kaveh; CyberAveng3rs; CyberAv3ngers; Soldiers of Solomon; Cyber Isnaad Front; Danfoss; AK-SM 800A; CyberbanNews
